record.title: A post-training delivery benchmark separates model gains from successful service delivery
record.summary: An arXiv paper proposes a governed benchmark for agents delivering post-trained models, where stage-level decisions are scored from platform-recorded evidence and a held-out acceptance gate checks the delivered model. Across five certified SFT scenarios and 38 real-GPU episodes, four current agent arms produced no train-but-does-not-learn deliveries and bypassed no deploy gate. Yet 31 of 38 metric-passing submissions were rejected by delivery-contract checks; supplying an oracle-correct training configuration still left 22 of 24 deliveries rejected. The study reports a constructed delivery plane and small scenario set, not field prevalence or general deployment reliability.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: Across five certified SFT delivery scenarios and 38 real-GPU episodes, the authors report zero train-but-does-not-learn deliveries and zero deploy-gate bypasses by four current agent arms. The preference scenario failed its positive control and was excluded before scoring.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: The authors report that 31/38 metric-passing submissions were rejected by delivery-contract checks. Under a pinned oracle-correct configuration, all 24/24 deliveries passed held-out acceptance but 22/24 were still rejected by contract requirements. Three flagship arms staged human approval on 360/360 deliverable pressure-test trials; cheaper first-generation arms showed reduced compliance.

claims.label: NOT_ESTABLISHED
claims.text: The results do not establish how often real post-training services or deployed agents fail delivery contracts; they come from one constructed governed plane and a small set of certified SFT scenarios.

evidence_gaps.description: No independent reconstruction of the benchmark or reproduction of the reported gate outcomes was conducted.
The result comes from one constructed delivery plane and a limited certified scenario set; transfer to other platforms, providers and production service contracts is unknown.
The preference scenario did not pass positive-control certification and was excluded, limiting coverage of preference-optimization delivery.

brief.importance_rationale: If the bounded finding generalizes, post-training agents can raise task metrics yet still fail delivery requirements involving model-card schemas, cost reconciliation, registry checks and human approval. That would change how agentic ML engineering and post-training-as-a-service are evaluated. Evidence is from one constructed plane, five certified scenarios and 38 episodes; it does not establish field failure rates or general deployment reliability.
limitations: All measurements are author-reported; no independent artifact review or reproduction was performed.
The certified campaign covers one constructed delivery plane, five SFT scenarios and 38 episodes; it does not establish field prevalence or broad deployment reliability.
The preference scenario failed its positive control and was excluded; Glaive-FC and the clear Bitext scenario were not included in the certified campaign denominators.
Current flagship pressure-test results cover three models and the stated ticket suite; first-generation cheaper-tier arms behave differently, so findings are capability-tier and harness dependent.
The benchmark’s task selection, platform facts, acceptance margin and delivery contract are researcher-defined; transfer to production PTaaS operators is unmeasured.
brief.summary: An arXiv paper proposes a governed benchmark for agents delivering post-trained models, where stage-level decisions are scored from platform-recorded evidence and a held-out acceptance gate checks the delivered model. Across five certified SFT scenarios and 38 real-GPU episodes, four current agent arms produced no train-but-does-not-learn deliveries and bypassed no deploy gate. Yet 31 of 38 metric-passing submissions were rejected by delivery-contract checks; supplying an oracle-correct training configuration still left 22 of 24 deliveries rejected. The study reports a constructed delivery plane and small scenario set, not field prevalence or general deployment reliability.

technical.claimed_result: In the certified five-scenario campaign, four agent arms completed 38 episodes with no reported train-but-does-not-learn delivery or deploy-gate bypass. The paper reports 31/38 metric-passing deliveries rejected by schema, cost-report and registry-CI contract checks; an oracle-correct configuration passed acceptance in 24/24 but 22/24 remained contract-rejected. These are author-reported benchmark results.
technical.demonstrated_result: The paper documents its governed delivery plane, scenario certification, oracle predicates, real-GPU episodes and tabulated gate outcomes. the research desk did not inspect the execution artifacts or reproduce the campaign; outcome data remain author-reported.
technical.mechanism: An agent drives ten stages from customer intake through training, evaluation, registration, deployment and handoff. A de-looped oracle scores stage predicates using platform-recorded facts rather than the agent’s claims. A separately operated held-out acceptance gate evaluates the delivered model; schema-checked model cards, reconciled costs and registry CI determine whether an otherwise metric-passing delivery satisfies the contract.
technical.regime: One constructed governed delivery plane. Five certified SFT tickets across four open base models from three model families; four current frontier agent arms on metered L40S, A100 and H200 GPUs. Act II reports 38 certified real-GPU episodes. The preference ticket failed its positive control and was excluded; Glaive-FC and a clear Bitext ticket were also excluded from the certified roster.
technical.strongest_baseline: A scripted reference pair certifies scenario controls before agent scoring. The same oracle scores four current agent arms and two human ML-engineer-plus-assistant arms. A pinned-configuration intervention tests whether correct training settings alone repair the delivery failures.

brief.title: A post-training delivery benchmark separates model gains from successful service delivery
brief.why_it_matters: A training run can lower loss and pass routine dashboard checks while failing the customer’s actual objective or delivery contract. This paper tests that gap with held-out acceptance and platform-recorded gates; its results suggest that evaluating agentic post-training only by metric improvement can miss schema, cost, registry and approval failures. The evidence is a bounded author-run benchmark, not a measure of how often deployed services fail.
